reply_text:
I found no dated AI prediction by Shane Legg from 2014. The record for that year is thin. After Google bought DeepMind in early 2014 he gave only a few public talks, and I couldn't read what he said at either of them.

**The two 2014 talks I found:**
- **ICCSW'14 keynote at Imperial College, "From Academia to Industry: The Story of Google DeepMind".** I opened the conference keynotes page. It has only an abstract written in the third person: Legg would cover DeepMind's history and moving from academia to industry, how Google DeepMind does research, and demos of its agents. There's no forecast in it. I also opened the matching Dagstuhl PDF, but it came back as raw PDF data and the printout was cut off, so I never read its text.
- **Kea UK event at New Zealand House, 17 Sep 2014.** YouTube showed a bot-protection page instead of the video, so I only got the description. It poses general questions about AI and contains none of his words. I couldn't get a recording or transcript.

**Other things that turned up:**
- A HuffPost UK article from 2014 retells his 2011 line about AI being his "number 1 risk for this century". That's a retelling of older words, and the site blocked the fetch, so I quote nothing from it.
- H+ Magazine reposted his machine superintelligence lecture in January 2014. A YouTube upload of the same lecture says it was given in 2009.
- His well-known 50% chance of AGI by 2028 comes from 2011 (a LessWrong Q&A) and from 2023 news coverage. I saw these only in search snippets and have listed them under other years.
- I opened the Oxford Martin School seminar page, but my own mistake lost what it returned, so I can't say what it held or when the seminar was.

I used 11 of the 12 searches and all 6 page openings, counting the one HuffPost blocked. My first script crashed while printing results after the first search went through, so I printed the stored results instead of running it again. I didn't run the last search because I had no openings left to check anything it found.
